Hi Ben / Redwood team,

Thanks again for walking us through the marketplace listing requirements last week. CloudSail is aiming to have a public listing and a co-marketing joint announcement in Q4; before we commit we need to validate a few technical and entitlements items so we don’t hit gating during the marketplace review. High-level asks: 

- Confirm whether Redwood supports per-tenant entitlement mapping for ISV connectors today (we need to map CloudSail SKUs -> Redwood entitlements).
- Clarify what telemetry hooks are required for listing (usage/events) and whether we need to expose any K8s-sidecar or can rely on your telemetry endpoint.
- Any mandatory security checklist items for GA listing (SOC2 artifacts / data residency confirmation).

I’m copying our engineering lead Samir and your product/technical contacts — would appreciate a short scoping doc or checklist we can honor. I attached our connector spec (api-contract-v1.2.pdf) and a draft interop checklist.

Thanks,

Thanks for the spec, Priya — skimmed the api-contract and interop-checklist. A few technical clarifications from our side so the Marketplace gating team can triage quickly: 

1) Entitlement mapping
- Redwood supports per-tenant entitlements via our entitlement API (token-based mapping). We do not currently ingest external SKU catalogs out-of-the-box; we can accept a CSV mapping at onboarding or build a one-time sync. For long-term we recommend integrating via our entitlement webhook so CloudSail events can be reflected in near-real-time.

2) Telemetry
- For listing we require anonymized usage metrics (request counts, error rates) and an event stream (success/failure). You can either push to our telemetry endpoint (preferred) or expose Prometheus metrics with a short-lived scraping job during the review window. No K8s-sidecar is mandatory.

3) Auth/SSO
- OAuth 2.0 is supported; if you need SAML-based enterprise SSO we’ll need to scope on a per-customer basis. For connector-to-connector API calls we recommend OAuth client credentials.

4) Data residency and logs
- We can provide retention and audit logs for the connector interactions; however, if CloudSail needs data to remain in a specific region (EU/APAC) we’ll need a Dedicated/Private deployment.

Open questions for CloudSail:
- Will you accept an initial CSV mapping for SKUs or do you want to implement the entitlement webhook?
- Any regulatory/regional constraints for user data in the telemetry payload?

I attached a short checklist with fields we’ll need completed (interop-checklist.xlsx) and the redlines I propose to the contract. I’ll be on the Thursday sync if scheduled.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Integration Engineer | Redwood Inference

Priya / team — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of product/program asks from the marketplace side so we can firm the go/no-go for Q4: 

- Entitlement approach: if CloudSail can accept an onboarding CSV for initial launch, we can proceed with a fast-track listing and then migrate to the webhook model in 6–8 weeks. Please confirm by Friday EOD.

- Telemetry: we need the anonymized usage payload by the reviewer; Karthik’s suggested push-to-endpoint is easiest for us. If that’s hard for you, flag now.

- Billing hook: for co-billing on the marketplace we need a mapping between CloudSail plan IDs and Redwood billing SKUs (sample CSV will do).

Tentative timeline (if answers are yes):
- Sept 5: complete CSV mapping + telemetry dev notes
- Sept 12: Redwood internal review (security + listing)
- Sept 19: soft listing + announcement window comms

I’ve created a short GH ticket and a Drive folder for artifacts (link below). If we get the CSV and telemetry samples by Friday we can keep to the schedule — otherwise we should push to late Oct.

Marissa Cole
